t: Which of the following conditions are not suitable for a spontaneous reaction?
s:
ΔG=ΔH−TΔS. Non-spontaneous means ΔG>0.
ΔH<0, ΔS>0: ΔG=(−)−T(+)=(−) always ⇒ always spontaneous.
ΔH<0, ΔS<0 at low T: ΔH dominates ⇒ΔG<0 ⇒ spontaneous at low T.
ΔH>0, ΔS<0: ΔG=(+)−T(−)=(+) always ⇒ never spontaneous at any temperature.
ΔH>0, ΔS>0 at high T: TΔS dominates ⇒ΔG<0 ⇒ spontaneous at high T.
Correct option: (3)
p: First Law and Basic Fundamentals of Thermodynamics

t:

[[img:f2cad46cb131]]
s:
Area under the P-V graph represents work done.
A process flowing left to right ⇒ positive work. A process flowing right to left ⇒ negative work.
From the graph: work done in a<0, work done in c>0 … (i)
A process at a higher level (further from x-axis) has greater magnitude of work ⇒ work in a> work in b (in magnitude) … (ii)
For maximum net positive work in a cycle:
Top process must flow left to right and be as far from the x-axis as possible ⇒ process c is ideal.
Bottom process must flow right to left and be as close to the x-axis as possible ⇒ process e is ideal.
The cycle c-e gives the maximum positive work done among all options.

Given molar specific heat at constant volume Cᵥ=3R/2, the ratio of specific heats is:
γ=1+R/Cᵥ=1+2/3=5/3
For an adiabatic process, the relationship between pressure and volume is P₁V₁^γ=P₂V₂^γ.
P₂=P₁(V₁/V₂)^γ
Substituting P₁=10⁵ N/m², V₁=6 L, and V₂=2 L:

Using the given value (3)^(5/3)=6.19:
P₂=6.19×10⁵ N/m²
The work done on the gas is given by W=(P₂V₂−P₁V₁)/(γ−1).
Converting volumes to standard units (1 L=10⁻³ m³):
W=((6.19×10⁵×2×10⁻³)−(10⁵×6×10⁻³))/(5/3−1)
W=(1238−600)/(2/3)
W=(638×3)/2
W=+957 J

t: A reaction that is spontaneous can be described as:
s:
A reaction that is spontaneous can be described as
proceeding without external influence once it has begun. TRUE. A spontaneous reaction has a tendency to proceed in the way it has begun. It is spontaneous when Gibbs free energy is negative.
releasing heat to the surroundings. FALSE. If the reaction is exothermic (enthalpy negative), one still has to take into account the effect of the entropy on Gibbs free energy.
proceeding in both the forward and reverse directions. FALSE. This just means that the reaction is reversible.
having the same rate in both the forward and reverse directions. FALSE. This is related to the kinetics but not the spontaneity.
So, the correct option is (d)
